name: Coagulation Disorders: Haemophilia, DIC and Liver Disease

reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Haemophilia bleeds deep and late; platelet defects bleed superficial and immediate
Haemophilia A is factor VIII, B is factor IX (Christmas disease)
Von Willebrand disease is the commonest inherited bleeding disorder
DIC consumes everything: platelets and fibrinogen fall while D dimer rises
reference.pathophysiology: Factor deficiency cripples thrombin generation so fibrin reinforcement fails after initial platelet plugs form, explaining delayed deep bleeding. Von Willebrand factor mediates platelet adhesion under shear and chaperones factor VIII, so its loss combines both bleeding styles. DIC is systemic thrombin generation triggered by tissue factor exposure or endothelial injury.
additionalDifferentials: Inherited versus acquired haemophilia from inhibitors
additionalInvestigations: APTT and PT with platelet count and bleeding pattern assessment
Factor VIII, IX and von Willebrand antigen and activity assays
D dimer, fibrinogen and film schistocytes for DIC scoring
